abstract: We build a labor market in which AI systems enter as workers: they apply for jobs, pass screenings, get hired, and get dismissed, alongside humans. Firms post vacancies, workers search with friction, and product demand slopes downward. Across 30 seeded runs per configuration, AI entry at 70% of the human wage raises unemployment by 4.1 percentage points (95% CI 3.5 to 4.6) and leaves 12.2 fewer humans employed (CI 10.5 to 13.9). Layoffs dominate when AI is much cheaper than humans: the layoff margin accounts for 7.2 of the lost jobs and reduced hiring for 5.0, though most dismissed workers find work again. A wider price gap reduces displacement, because cheap AI makes firms expand: at price parity, with zero dismissals, the unemployment effect is largest at 9.2 points (CI 8.6 to 9.9), all of it through hiring. That parity result survives cutting AI applications from five per period to one. Demand elasticity decides how many workers AI displaces. Screening changes who gets hired and leaves the displacement total unchanged.

ob.ai_reason: AI作为劳动力的搜索匹配模型，AI核心，劳动市场相关
ob.tldr: 研究构建搜索匹配劳动力市场模型，模拟AI作为劳动者进入市场对就业的影响。30次种子运行显示：AI以70%人类工资进入使失业率上升4.1个百分点；当AI远便宜于人类时，裁员是主因（贡献7.2个岗位流失）；而价格持平时零裁员但招聘减少导致9.2个百分点的失业率上升。需求弹性决定替代程度，筛选机制只改变雇佣结构而不改变替代总量。

title: Displacement Is Endogenous: AI Workers in a Search-and-Matching Labor Market
title_zh: 替代是内生的：搜索匹配劳动力市场中的AI工作者
